newsitem.title: UK: London taxi drivers head for stock market.
newsitem.headline: London taxi drivers head for stock market.

text.p: London taxi drivers are heading for the stock market after backing the flotation of Computer Cab Co Limited, Britain's largest licensed taxi operator.
The licensed Taxi Drivers' Association (LTDA) said on Monday that over 60 percent of its members had voted for the planned flotation on London's secondary Alternative Investment Market.

LTDA general secretary Bob Oddy said he was "delighted that good sense has prevailed," despite objections from a minority of members at a meeting on Sunday. Computer Cab, a wholly owned subsidiary of the LTDA plans to list its shares in December.
The London taxi firm is hoping to raise around half of the 7.5 million pounds ($12.5 million) needed to set up the UK's first satellite based automatic taxi location system.

The system is designed to cut waiting times for London's fleet of black cabs and reduce the amount of distance drivers cover before picking up a fare. A number of London's famously outspoken "cabbies" have objected that they will be contributing to the capital cost of the system without receiving any equity in the company.
The drivers also said they were never informed of the need to sell off part of the equity in order to complete the project. ($1=.5994 Pound)
